data.narrative:
Improbable Defence is a Growth-stage defence and security company that has raised $703M to date. The comp universe for this sector includes two public peers (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and eight private companies, with notable private comparables including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable methodology. Stage-Progression, which applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement, yields $844M. A peer-median approach could not be applied: while 23 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters for stage-alignment, adjacent-stage positioning, and similar valuation tier produced fewer than three datapoints in any category, making aggregate peer multiples unreliable without introducing material bias.

The triangulation produces a valuation range of $717M (low) to $970M (high), with a median of $844M. This range reflects the limited methodological basis—only one quantitative method applied—and underscores a key uncertainty: the absence of sufficient same-stage and same-tier Defence & Security comparables constrains the precision of relative valuation. Any conclusion requires weighting Stage-Progression evidence against qualitative differentiation within the defence tech landscape, where public and private peer multiples may diverge substantially from growth-stage norms. Further peer data or transaction evidence in this segment would materially improve conviction.
